name: AndyClaw
vibe_summary: A full OpenClaw-style agentic AI assistant packaged as a single Android APK, with deep ethOS/crypto-wallet integration on the dGEN1 phone. It pairs an on-device Qwen2.5-1.5B local model with autonomous heartbeat-driven background operation.
best_for: dGEN1/ethOS phone owners wanting native wallet-integrated AI
Android users wanting an on-device agent without a server
Crypto users who want AI-managed micro-payment wallets
avoid_if: You need a desktop or server-based assistant
You are uncomfortable granting an AI shell and device control
You want a large, mature community and plugin ecosystem
openclaw_advantages: Runs natively on Android as a single APK, no server or PC needed
On-device local LLM (Qwen2.5-1.5B) works fully offline
Deep crypto wallet and XMTP integration on ethOS
Autonomous OS-managed heartbeat for background operation
openclaw_disadvantages: Far smaller community and ecosystem (90 stars vs hundreds of thousands)
Full feature set locked to ethOS/dGEN1 hardware
High-risk permissions (shell, device control, wallet) with limited sandboxing
Mobile-only; no desktop or multi-channel support
confidence_summary: README and commit history give strong evidence of architecture and activity, but community sentiment data is essentially noise (Reddit matches are unrelated), so popularity and reception scores are uncertain.

overview_markdown:
AndyClaw is an open-source (GPL-3.0) Android port of the OpenClaw concept, built by Freedom Factory for the dGEN1 phone and ethOS but functional on any Android device. It ships as a single APK with an agentic tool-use loop supporting up to 20 chained tool calls per turn, letting the AI control device hardware, send messages, manage files, run shell commands, and execute multi-step tasks autonomously.

The app operates in two modes: on ethOS it unlocks a privileged mode with wallet signing authentication, multi-chain transaction support (Ethereum, Optimism, Polygon, Arbitrum, Base), XMTP messaging, full device control, and an AI-controlled sub-account wallet for micro-payments. On stock Android it runs in an open mode with a bundled local Qwen2.5-1.5B model or user-supplied OpenRouter/tinfoil API keys, plus Termux integration and ClawHub community skills.

A distinguishing feature is its heartbeat architecture: the OS (or a foreground service on stock Android) periodically wakes the agent to act autonomously in the background, with persistent heartbeat logging and long-term memory across sessions. Recent commits show active hardening work — atomic backup restores, FTS index rebuilds, and binder IPC fixes — indicating a maturing but still fast-moving codebase. Compared to OpenClaw, it trades ecosystem size and multi-platform reach for deep mobile and crypto-native integration.
